dimensions.note: A private key reaches a short-lived ssh-agent over stdin; a password goes through a temporary askpass helper and an environment variable; neither appears in ssh argv (tested). Secret fields are sensitive-marked. 2026.10.17.2: upload no longer sends the expected content SHA-256 to the remote; the remote prints the destination's own SHA-256 and mode after the rename and the comparison runs locally, so no content-derived digest appears on any spawned argv or in remote script text for upload (probe and write), exec or execPipeline (new unit test asserts no 64-hex string on any argv). exec returns only exit code and SHA-256 of stdout/stderr; raw output is stored only in the sensitive execution resource when return_output is set. Residual MEDIUM (terra, carried from 2026.10.17.1; raised as HIGH in the delta round and refuted as a regression): the SHA-256 of low-entropy output or content returned in results and resources could be guessed; hashes in place of raw content is the design the run rulings require. Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: the CLI prints literal sensitive arguments, so README examples use vault references only and never --json. 2026.10.17.3: exec gains an optional stdin that is streamed to ssh stdin and never placed on argv, so it may carry secrets; the no-options argv is byte-identical to the fe0139f0 transport (unit test and scripted comparison), and no content hash reaches argv.
Each method logs once with structured placeholders (host, port, exit code, changed, key count); no secret, argv or output in log fields.

A remote non-zero exit is returned as data; every OpenSSH exit 255 maps to a typed SshError (host key, auth, unreachable, transport), live-verified. Typed SshConfigError for bad policy, pins that match nothing for the host, and a supplied pin that disagrees with the recorded pin. Output over max_output_bytes kills the child with a typed error. upload now fails with a typed 'did not converge' SshError when the post-rename hash or mode read back differs. Residual MEDIUM (terra, new in 2026.10.17.2): the post-rename check reads the first stdout token, so a target whose forced-command wrapper prints to stdout fails upload after the rename; it fails closed, never a false success. Residual MEDIUM (carried): a Linux target without sha256sum/shasum fails only after the rename. 2026.10.17.3: timeoutMs kills the local ssh and raises SshError kind timeout, never a partial success; maxOutputBytes caps stdout and sets truncated instead of throwing; stderr is bounded separately by max_output_bytes and throws over it, so ssh diagnostics stay whole and every exit 255 still classifies (live: 12/12 failure cells throw at caps 16/64/4096). Residual MEDIUM (terra): remote stderr is not cut to the caller's stdout cap, by design (documented). On timeout the remote command keeps running (documented).

65 unit tests with an injected runner, clock and sleep (no process or socket), including a new test that no content-derived 64-hex string reaches any spawned argv or script text, and upload fakes that return the post-rename hash and mode. Live end-to-end matrix: 23/23 on 2026.10.17.1 (on stable). For 2026.10.17.2 the 17 non-upload cells carry over (code path byte-identical); the six upload cells (3, 3b, 10, X2, X3, X4) are pending re-run on 2026.10.17.2, which beta allows; they must pass before promotion to stable. 2026.10.17.3: 80 unit tests, including a byte-identical no-options argv test, real-sh runner tests for stdin, timeout, truncation and the separate stderr cap. Container sshd round trip (ubuntu:24.04, pinned key over ssh-agent) at 5cc589d: failure cells throw at caps 16/64/4096, insecure_tofu first use at cap 64 runs with the warning whole, yes truncation under 400 ms, NUL, 4 MiB and 64 MiB stdin match, a timeout mid-stdin raises kind timeout; receipts in the LOGBOOK.

upload probes the destination SHA-256 and mode and skips the write (no new resource version) when both match (probe unchanged from 2026.10.17.1, live-verified there); a mode-only change goes through the temp-file mv -T path, and the post-rename read-back now checks both hash and mode locally. insecure_tofu pins are committed only after the transport succeeds. Residual MEDIUM (carried, downgraded under the run rulings): two simultaneous first-use calls can race on the pin write.

Built on the OpenSSH client, ssh-agent/ssh-add and ssh-keyscan with -F /dev/null and IdentityFile=none, so the operator's ssh config is never consulted. upload requires GNU mv -T and fails closed on non-Linux targets.

Temporary known_hosts, askpass helper and ssh-agent are removed or killed in finally (tested). Remote output is streamed with a cap (default 10 MiB, max 100 MiB). Residual MEDIUM (astra, terra): ssh-keyscan output is not capped; scan output is small and the cap is a follow-up. 2026.10.17.3: a truncated or timed-out exec kills ssh and stops reading instead of draining an endless writer; stdin and readers share one Promise.all and the abort listener is removed in finally.

Manifest: @randybias/ssh-host 2026.10.17.2 (model version literals match), two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt. exec and upload descriptions start DESTRUCTIVE. Fixtures use RFC 5737 addresses and low-entropy synthetic host keys; leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Residual LOW (astra, carried): the exec and upload descriptions describe return_output and mode-only changes inaccurately. LOW (astra, delta): a redundant exact-hash assertion in the new test. 2026.10.17.3: manifest and model version literals 2026.10.17.3; upgrades is a literal array on the exported model (dry run free of the version-bump warning). The model's own exec does not expose the new options.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; host, user, port, remote path and mode carry grammars; argv rejects NUL and every word is POSIX-quoted, live-verified against injection. host_keys and argv are bounded. host_key_policy is required with no default; strict requires pins. Residual MEDIUM (astra): argv words have no allowlist grammar beyond NUL; quoting is the defence for a generic exec primitive.
execution, upload and connection resources: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 10.

Transport primitive with three action methods: exec, upload and wait_connection. It owns no remote resource lifecycle, so there is no create/delete; consumers (server-host, wireguard-mesh, k0s-cluster) own that.

Policy, pins and paths are validated before any spawn; strict without pins, pins for another host and a pin that disagrees with the record are refused before connecting. upload refuses a directory, symlink, trailing slash or dot component before writing and re-checks around the rename (mv -T, symlink and directory refusal unchanged in 2026.10.17.2).

Length-prefixed components avoid collisions: the TOFU pin is connection-h<len>-<host>-p<port> (host+port, known_hosts semantics, so a second user is verified against the same pin); exec and upload evidence add u<len>-<user>.
Methods read only this model's own connection resource for the pin; every target arrives as method arguments, so one generic definition serves any host.

2026.10.17.2 is a point release of 2026.10.17.1 with no schema, argument, resource or instance-name change; data written by 2026.10.17.1 is read unchanged. The vendored _lib/ssh.ts blob is now fe0139f08c42e3fdae0061b9688fb5c534174957; vendors resync to it. 2026.10.17.3 is additive: no model schema, argument, resource or instance-name change; an identity upgrade entry is declared. The vendored _lib/ssh.ts blob is now 8f132c4329c9e64bed686731cd5a0e02980194ea (one file, 1250 lines, so vendors copy it byte for byte); vendors re-vendor one by one.
